title: Krylov Complexity and Entropy of Composite Quantum Systems
abstract: We investigate the behaviour of Krylov complexity as the number of degrees of freedom of a quantum system increases. Specifically, we show that for tensor products of commuting subsystems, the leading excess complexity is controlled by a weighted variance of the subsystem Lanczos coefficients. This provides a quantitative measure of dynamical heterogeneity and a precise characterization of synchronous evolution. We also show that Krylov entropy is able to disambiguate the information associated with subsystems composition from that generated by dynamical mismatch, and that the same Lanczos variance controls the leading mismatch contribution to both complexity and the entropy. Our results establish excess complexity and Krylov entropy as complementary probes of the emergence of collective dynamics in large quantum systems.

bite.hook: Leading excess Krylov complexity in composite quantum systems is directly controlled by subsystem Lanczos variance.
tldr: Studied how Krylov complexity and entropy behave as quantum degrees of freedom scale up in composite systems.
Analyzed tensor products of commuting subsystems via Lanczos coefficients to isolate dynamical mismatch.
Proved a weighted variance of Lanczos coefficients controls excess complexity and disambiguates system composition.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding how quantum complexity grows across subsystems helps pinpoint when collective behaviors emerge in many-body quantum devices and black-hole models.
bite.eli5: Imagine an orchestra where each musician plays their own rhythm. If everyone's internal tempo drifts apart, a simple mathematical variance captures exactly how chaotic the combined performance becomes over time.

glossary.shortDef: A measure of how an operator or state spreads across an orthogonal basis generated by time evolution.
glossary.eli5Def: A score for how deeply information scatters into harder-and-harder-to-reach corners of a quantum system.

glossary.shortDef: Parameters from the Lanczos algorithm that characterize quantum operator spreading.
glossary.eli5Def: A set of numbers describing the step-by-step difficulty of pushing quantum information outward.

glossary.shortDef: Entropy computed from the distribution of an evolving state over Krylov basis elements.
glossary.eli5Def: A measure of how evenly quantum information is smeared across available states as time passes.
